overview: The week of October 12-19 was dominated by a sweeping memory safety, lifetime, and locking overhaul from Alexei Starovoitov spanning a 43-patch v2 series and a 16-patch v3 followup, addressing extension program safety, dynptr write semantics, skb cloning, and packet-pointer lifetime across the BPF subsystem. Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi continued refining BPF arenas with a v5 16-patch series adding __arena and __nullable BTF type tags alongside libbpf auto-binding, and posted a new patch enforcing that signed programs cannot carry CO-RE relocations. Alexei also introduced unwind_goto and unwind_exit instructions for structured BPF exception handling, with x86 and arm64 JIT backends updated accordingly.

patches.title: bpf: Don't take a program with a target program for an iterator
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: This is patch 01/16 of the "Memory safety, lifetime and locking fixes (followups)" v3 series, a targeted refinement of the 43-patch v2 series posted earlier in the week. The larger effort addresses a wide class of BPF memory safety issues: preventing extensions from reaching past their target program's context, enforcing that sleepable programs retain ownership of values from a dead owner, refusing extension prologues for incompatible function signatures, and using memmove() instead of unsafe direct writes when storing bytes into skb and xdp_buff via dynptrs. The followup series distills these changes to a tighter 16-patch set after review feedback.

patches.title: bpf: Add syscall common attrs support for link_create
patches.author: Leon Hwang
patches.summary: This 6-patch series (v2) adds common syscall attribute support to the BPF link_create path, specifically targeting XDP links. It introduces a new bpf_link_create_log API in libbpf that surfaces log output when link creation fails, replacing the now-retired bpf_xdp_link_attach_failed tracepoint. The change improves debuggability of XDP link attachment failures by providing structured error information through the standard log mechanism. Companion selftests verify the new log behavior end-to-end.

patches.title: bpf: Refuse CO-RE relocations for a signed program
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: This 2-patch series (v1) adds a verifier check that rejects CO-RE (Compile Once, Run Everywhere) relocations when loading a signed BPF program. Signed programs rely on a stable binary digest for integrity verification, but CO-RE relocations patch the program bytecode at load time, invalidating any pre-computed signature. The fix ensures the two features remain mutually exclusive, preventing a class of security policy bypass where a signed but CO-RE-relocated program could differ from what was originally signed.

patches.title: bpf: Check exclusive maps once the program digest is final
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: This 16-patch series (v5, "Fix some arena paper cuts") addresses several usability issues with BPF arenas. Key changes include new __arena and __nullable BTF type tags recognized by the verifier, correct handling of loads of __arena pointer struct members, and libbpf automatically binding an object's arena map to every program it contains. Additional patches fix arena base register setup to only occur in functions that actually use it and improve BTF rendering of the arena type tag with its address space. The series ships with extensive selftests covering all new behaviors.

patches.title: sched: add BPF-based per-cgroup NUMA balancing mode selection
patches.author: Yafang Shao
patches.summary: This RFC 5-patch series (v3) introduces BPF kfuncs that allow selecting the NUMA balancing mode on a per-cgroup basis from a BPF program. It adds scheduler helpers for NUMA balancing and exposes them as kfuncs callable from sched BPF programs, enabling workload-aware NUMA policy without kernel recompilation. The series includes a bugfix for a stale get_pref_llc() stub when CONFIG_SCHED_CACHE is disabled and ships with selftests for the new kfuncs.

patches.title: bpf: Add unwind_goto and unwind_exit insns
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: This 5-patch series (v2) introduces two new BPF instructions, unwind_goto and unwind_exit, to support structured exception-like unwinding from BPF programs. The instructions allow a program to jump to a cleanup label on error without the overhead of a full C++ exception unwind table, and the JIT backends for both x86 and arm64 are updated to emit the corresponding native sequences. A companion testcase adds a C++ BPF program that uses C++ exceptions, exercising the new mechanism end-to-end.

patches.title: bpf: Protect the struct_ops association with a spinlock
patches.author: Qiliang Yuan
patches.summary: This 4-patch series (v5) fixes a use-after-free race in struct_ops maps that manifested as a flaky assoc_in_timer selftest. The fix dissociates struct_ops programs before the map enters its RCU grace period and protects the association state with a spinlock, eliminating the window where a running program could access a map that has already begun teardown. A new selftest directly exercises freeing a struct_ops map under a concurrently running program.

patches.title: bpf: Refuse the prologue for an extension if callers keep packet pointers
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: This patch tightens verifier safety for BPF extension programs: if any caller of a freplace target keeps live packet pointers at the call site, the verifier now refuses to insert a prologue for the extension. This prevents the extension from operating on a stale packet pointer that was invalidated by the prologue's helper calls, closing a potential memory safety hole in XDP and tc programs that use function replacement.

patches.title: bpf: Determine freplace staticness from BTF linkage
patches.author: KaFai Wan
patches.summary: This 4-patch series (v3, "Fix selftests fails with clang23") addresses test failures caused by clang23's stricter interpretation of BTF linkage. The primary kernel change teaches the verifier to determine whether a freplace target is static by inspecting its BTF linkage type rather than relying on other heuristics. Companion patches fix log expectations in precision backtracking and stack argument pruning tests that diverged between GCC and clang23's output format.

patches.title: bpf: Reject packet dynptr slices in mutating helpers and subprograms
patches.author: Ren Wei
patches.summary: This 2-patch series (v2) adds a verifier check that rejects packet dynptr slices when passed to helpers or subprograms that could mutate packet data. Mutating helpers may reallocate the underlying packet buffer, invalidating any existing pointers derived from the dynptr slice. The patch prevents a use-after-free class of bugs by teaching the verifier to track when a dynptr refers to packet memory and refusing the unsafe combination at verification time.

patches.title: libbpf: Prefer mounted tracefs over debugfs
patches.author: Eduard Zateev
patches.summary: This single patch updates libbpf's tracefs discovery logic to prefer a separately mounted tracefs filesystem over tracefs exposed through debugfs. On systems where tracefs is mounted independently at /sys/kernel/tracing, relying on the debugfs path at /sys/kernel/debug/tracing can fail if debugfs is not mounted. The fix checks for a standalone tracefs mount first and only falls back to the debugfs path if no independent mount is found.
